subject: Unexpected rate-limit rejections affecting OptimaApps — recovery checklist
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@optimaapps.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-14T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: sudden 429s from 06:00-07:30 PST — our production is throttled

Hi Grace,

We're seeing a large number of 429s starting ~06:00 PST that affected most of our production workers for about 90 minutes. Error rate peaked ~25% for requests to text-generation endpoints. We restarted a few workers and traffic dropped, but the issue looks platform-side as the same payloads that previously succeeded are now failing with 429. Attached are a small sample of request/response lines and timestamps.

Can you confirm whether anything changed on your side? This impacted our onboarding flow and a small batch job. We're starting to roll back to a cached fallback but need a timeline for resolution.

Thanks,
Liam
Ops Lead, OptimaApps

Hi Liam — thanks for the report and the logs. I'm escalating this now to our on-call infra/serving team and will keep you posted every 30 minutes until resolved. Immediate steps we're taking: 

- Triage: Ben (serving) is looking at tenant quota mapping and recent deploys.
- Short-term mitigation: we can apply a temporary tenant quota override for OptimaApps to restore in-flight traffic.
- Monitoring: we'll stream a filtered logs view to your ops email and post updates to our status page.

Can you confirm whether you were routing traffic through the EU region for any batch jobs this morning? That helps us rule out cross-region config issues.

I'll follow up in 30 mins with the first update.

Best,

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, Liam O'Connor <liam@optimaapps.com>
Date: 2026-02-14T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: sudden 429s from 06:00-07:30 PST — our production is throttled

Grace / team — quick technical summary from the on-call investigation: 

Root cause candidate: a recent rollout of a quota normalization change (converting legacy token units to the new "unit-v2" scale) contained an off-by-10 divisor applied to tenant overrides created during a migration batch. That caused per-tenant effective quotas to be 10x lower than intended for tenants with a legacy override present. The change was deployed 02/14 02:45 UTC and coincides with the start of the spike.

Immediate actions taken (09:00 PST):
- Applied temporary override to OptimaApps to match pre-rollout quota (override applied manually via internal admin CLI).
- Scoped a hotfix branch to revert the normalization for tenant overrides and queued for canary rollout.
- Added logging to emit the effective quota per-tenant at request time to validate the fix.

I've attached the exact CLI commands I used to override OptimaApps and a short checklist for rollback/validation. Please consider this emergency mitigation — we'll follow with a permanent patch and test plan.

Ben
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: override-commands.txt (plain text)

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-02-14T12:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: sudden 429s from 06:00-07:30 PST — our production is throttled

Hi Liam — following up to summarize the customer-facing recovery checklist and next steps. We want to make sure you have everything you need and to schedule a short postmortem review.

Customer recovery checklist (what we did / what we recommend):

1) Temporary quota override applied at 09:00 PST (we kept it at the pre-deploy level).
2) Validation: we pulled a sample of requests after override; error rate dropped from ~25% to <1% within 12 minutes.
3) Suggested action for OptimaApps: continue traffic ramp for 30 minutes, watch for any anomalous error spikes, and report any 429s to ops@redwood.ai with request ids.
4) Follow-up: we'll run a canary of the normalization hotfix in our staging cluster and then a narrow canary in prod. We will not re-enable the normalization change for tenant overrides until after a full postmortem and test sweep.
5) Credits: if you'd like, we can open a request for service credits for the impacted window (we'll need the HubSpot deal id).

Proposed schedule for postmortem: 2026-02-16 10:00 PST (30 minutes). If that doesn't work, suggest alternatives.

Attached is a short PDF checklist and a sanitized log bundle we'll upload to a temporary S3 link.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Neha / Grace / Ben — thanks for the fast response and for the override. We've ramped traffic back up and verified that the 429s have stopped. Attached are our post-recovery logs and a timeline from our side; error rate is back to normal. We appreciate the transparency and the proposed postmortem time works for me.

One ask before the postmortem: can the team share the exact roll-forward plan for the normalization change and what additional guardrails will be added to prevent a similar miscalculation? A short bullet list in advance would help our engineering review.

Thanks again — appreciate the quick mitigation.

Liam
Ops Lead, OptimaApps
